still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind.

The eleven 2034 state bans on weight-indication incretin prescribing under age 12 (Texas, Florida, Louisiana, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Indiana, Ohio, Utah, Missouri, West Virginia) are unchanged, no state has added or repealed one, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 42.5% ever-used minus 32.1% current leaves 10.4% of adults who used and are off now. About 48% of current users are on a second or later course (15.4 points, up from 45% because the 2035 shortage forced a break on millions who then restarted). Another 3.4 points have cycled and are off again, so (15.4 + 3.4) / 42.5 ≈ 44.2% of ever-users have cycled. The other 7.0 points stopped once and have not restarted. First-course current users are 16.7 points (parent 15.4), which includes most of the 5.0 points of new ever-users. This fits one-year persistence of about one-third on full-dose regimens and ~55% on low-dose plans, with restart at 36–47% within a year, plus a shortage-driven involuntary stop-and-restart wave. Age check: 0.20×20.5 + 0.33×32.7 + 0.24×43 + 0.23×30 = 4.1 + 10.8 + 10.3 + 6.9 ≈ 32.1. Income thirds average 32.1. 32.1% of ~276M adults is ~88.6M users, up ~12M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~12.0M (13.5%, down from 14.5M after employers retreated), Medicare ~15.0M (17%), Medicaid ~3.6M (4%), legitimate branded cash ~29.0M (33%), compounded ~9.0M (10%, regrown from near zero after semaglutide went on the shortage list in May 2035), imported or counterfeit ~20.0M (23%). Sum 88.6M. Gray plus compounded is ~29M (33%). The legitimate cash channel breaks down as ~12.6M weight users, ~8.6M longevity plans, ~3.6M calm/focus, ~1.5M Reset, ~1.6M alcohol-reduction and ~1.1M nicotine-cessation fills (~0.6M since the April 2036 approval). Sum 29.0M. ~17M current users have a BMI under 30 and ~5.5M under 25. Adult obesity is ~31.2%. ~18% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. ~1.3M users also take bimagrumab. Pediatric: ~1.1% of under-18s are on a drug (12–17s ~2.5%, the rise mostly compounded product for teens). Under-12 use is flat at ~0.12% outside ban states. ~53% of children live with a current user, and ~7.2M live with a parent who regained after stopping, up because of shortage-forced breaks.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~15.0M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.0M × ~$225 average net/month × 12 ≈ $40.5B a year in gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B. Users grew; the average net held at $225 because the shortage stopped the 3–5% annual drift. Medicare is the one payer whose price did not rise in the shock. Medicaid: 7 states still cover weight-loss use, with ~3.6M users mostly on diabetes codes. Some state formularies moved semaglutide users to tirzepatide during the shortage under existing PA rules.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $5–30 a month after India's B2C export registration took effect in Jan 2035, which added paperwork and shifted volume toward registered exporters but did not stop parcels. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue, 'reta' and now 'cagri' vials sell for $25–80 through research-peptide fronts. Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide runs CAD 50–85 and BRL 170–290. India and China supply ~70% of world incretin volume, and Chinese API supplies most US compounders.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The shock was a single plant. In Mar 2035 Novo halted semaglutide API production at Clayton, NC after FDA inspectors found endotoxin excursions, and it recalled 41 lots of Wegovy pill and Rybelsus. The oral peptide uses many times the API of the injectable, so the pill took most of the hit. The FDA listed semaglutide in shortage in May 2035, which made 503A/503B compounding legal again. Allocation pricing (Jul 2035) raised TrumpRx Wegovy pill maintenance from $179 to $249, starting doses from $149 to $199, and injectable Wegovy from $229 to $299. Lilly absorbed spillover demand: Foundayo starting doses held at $149 (the market floor), maintenance rose $199 → $229, Zepbound went to $299–329 and retatrutide $299 → $349. Amgen held MariTide at $219 but closed direct-cash enrolment Jul–Dec 2035; ~6.5M users remain (~5.0M in employer clinic tracks). The weighted average branded cash price rose from ~$205 to ~$250. Semaglutide came off the shortage list in Feb 2036, but ~9M people stayed on compounded product at $119–199. Telehealth '503A personalised' formulas add B12 or glycine to claim clinical difference, and compounded retatrutide and cagrilintide from Chinese API ($179–249) are illegal and openly sold. FDA warning letters number in the hundreds. Employer weight coverage fell from 29% to 21% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2035), and coverage concentrated on diabetes and CV codes. Another ~11% cover only through monitored tracks (6.3M enrollees, inside the 12.0M commercial). LSA reimbursement of calm and Reset fees slipped from 19% to 15% of large employers. Lilly's 'Strong' bundle (retatrutide plus monthly clinic bimagrumab) is $899 cash. Bimagrumab list stays $1,150.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct (bimagrumab; label updated Feb 2036 with 72-week lean-mass and BMD data; sold co-packaged with retatrutide as Lilly 'Strong')
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, Aug 2033)
smoking and vaping cessation in adults (oral semaglutide, approved Apr 2036)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, with growth-monitoring language; barred for weight indication by statute in eleven states)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial read out 2035, positive on a narrower effect, label retained)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity microdosing by adults without obesity (~8.6M licensed plus a large compounded and gray share)
compulsion 'Reset' plans for betting, shopping, porn and screens (~1.5M licensed)
scheduled 'drug holidays' and dose-floor titration to manage blunting, now standard clinical advice
compounded and gray 'reta', 'cagri' and fake 'bima' stacks in gym and longevity communities
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The muscle-preserving-combo driver is realised through existing products in a new form, as the approval rules require. Bimagrumab (approved Jun 2034) got a Feb 2036 label update adding 72-week DXA data: lean-mass loss cut from ~35% to ~15% of weight lost, and a modest hip-BMD benefit. There are no fracture-outcome data. Lilly launched 'Strong', a co-packaged retatrutide 12 mg plus monthly clinic bimagrumab programme, in Mar 2036 and filed a co-formulated monthly injection in Jan 2036. It is under review, and approval is not possible before 2037. Nicotine: Novo filed oral semaglutide for smoking and vaping cessation in Jan 2035 on two phase 3 trials (~2.1× continuous abstinence vs placebo at 24 weeks, less than varenicline head-to-head), and the FDA approved it in Apr 2036. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out positive in 2035 for the obesity-plus-CVD population, and no non-CVD filing has been made. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 reads out no earlier than late 2036; there is no compulsion indication. Implants remain in phase 2. No new triple-agonist molecule has been approved. Novo's Clayton line restarted in Dec 2035 and is at ~80% capacity. Net prices stopped drifting down in 2035 and branded cash now sits at ~$149–349.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens. Drug holidays added a new pattern: restarting at full dose after two or more missed weeks without re-titrating causes ED visits for vomiting and dehydration, which peaked in Q4 2035 as shortage users came back.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. A 2035 label update tells patients to re-titrate after missing more than two weeks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute cases rose with retatrutide 12 mg and Strong volume, and per-user risk is unchanged.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis. The first EPI bellwether trial (2035) ended in a defence verdict on causation for that plaintiff's timeline.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR is ~1.3 in users 65+ after 2+ years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Shortage-forced cycling added to the cycled population. Bimagrumab reduces lean-mass loss on DXA, but no fracture-outcome data exist. The ~1.3M on bimagrumab are mostly younger, insured or upper-income, not the 65+ cyclers who carry the fracture risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; bimagrumab label updated Feb 2036 with surrogate data only.

safety_ledger.effect: NAION (non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy) and optic-nerve injury
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A pooled Medicare–VA–Nordic target-trial emulation (Jun 2035) found HR ~2.1 at weight-loss doses and ~2.6 on retatrutide 12 mg, with a dose gradient and no clear signal at low doses. Absolute risk is still low: ~0.4 excess cases per 10,000 person-years overall and ~1.5 in users 60+ with diabetes, or roughly 3,000–4,000 excess cases a year nationally at current exposure. Gray users get no labelling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class warning in Warnings and Precautions (Sep 2035) across all GLP-1-containing products, following EMA's earlier very-rare listing. It advises stopping on sudden painless vision loss and an eye exam before starting for patients with prior NAION or a 'disc at risk'. Not boxed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the nicotine trials.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% vs ~3% at weight-loss doses and ~10–11% on retatrutide. The first interim from the NIH normal-weight cohort (2036) suggests ~4–5% at low doses vs 3%, with wide intervals. The shortage acted as an unplanned withdrawal: mood scores in a Kaiser cohort of users forced off in 2035 rose within 3–6 weeks, then returned on restart, which strengthens the case for causation without proving it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FTC–FDA consent orders on marketing claims remain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. The 2035 shortage created the largest synchronised regain cohort yet, concentrated among Wegovy-pill cash users and bottom-third gray users.
B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Compounded B12 blends mask B12 deficiency but not iron. Low ferritin persists in adolescent girls.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide. Partial recovery in about half of people who stop for 12+ months. The tirzepatide excess is still non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (Mar 2031); tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~17M current users have a BMI under 30. The shortage and normalised holidays mean intermittent dosing is now the commonest real-world pattern, which no trial studied. The NIH cohort's first interim (2036) shows no new organ signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH cohort ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~71,000 by mid-2036. Compounded-vial dosing errors (units vs mg) returned with legal compounding in 2035. No new mass insulin-substitution event occurred, but there were ~300 hypoglycaemia ED visits from mislabelled 'reta' in 2035. 'Bima' research vials tested by state labs contained no antibody in 88% of samples. Poison-centre calls are ~8× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Hundreds of FDA warning letters to 503A pharmacies and telehealth sellers after semaglutide left the shortage list in Feb 2036. India's B2C export registration took effect in Jan 2035. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters persists at 48 months with no catch-up yet. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA label monitoring retained; eleven state under-12 bans unchanged; EMA specialist-initiation restriction retained.

safety_ledger.effect: Activin-receptor blockade effects (bimagrumab): muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne, lipase and lipid changes; long-term effects of combined use unknown
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Muscle spasm in ~25% early in treatment and acne in ~10%. Reproductive and cardiac effects of long-term activin blockade in younger users are uncharacterised. Strong-bundle users skew 30–50 and lean.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; PMR for a 5-year safety registry.

food_and_beverage.state: ~50% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–17% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. The shortage produced a measurable 'shortage bump': snack volume rose ~2–3% in Q3–Q4 2035 in Wegovy-pill-heavy zips before fading. Zip-code planning by user density is standard at Walmart and Kroger. The longevity and 'muscle' aisle grows with creatine, leucine and 'activin-support' supplements that are unregulated and mostly inert.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~19% from 2025 and beer ~12%. Q3 2035 brought a small uptick during the shortage, attributed by Diageo to 'interrupted therapy'. AUD fills are now ~1.6M. Tobacco and vape makers feel the newer pressure: Altria and the large vape distributors flag the April 2036 cessation approval as a headwind, though cigarette volumes were already falling ~8% a year and the drug's effect is not yet separable.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat and checks smaller. Portion tiers are standard. The shortage briefly lifted late-night QSR traffic in lower-income markets. Upscale chains in Scottsdale and Charlotte market 'Strong menus', high-protein plates timed to bimagrumab clinic days.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. One more regional chain liquidated in 2035, though stretch and resale revenue rose during the regain wave. 'Lifted-body' tailoring and structured athletic wear now cut for a muscled, lean silhouette. Mass retailers keep zip-coded size runs and wider ranges in low-density zips.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Premium DXA-plus-coaching clinics became Strong infusion sites, and the $899 bundle plus coaching runs $1,100–1,400 a month. Budget chains' $39 lean-mass add-ons are standard. Planet Fitness-tier gyms report members on compounded stacks asking staff about 'bima' vials.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage fell from 29% to 21%, and coverage concentrates on diabetes, CV and OSA codes. Pharmacy trend ~+7% in 2035 as shortage-era switching to tirzepatide and retatrutide raised unit costs. Adherence differentials persist under the 2027 guidance, but fewer firms bother now that fewer cover the drug. LSA calm and Reset reimbursement slipped to 15% of large employers. Part D premiums rose again.

pharma.state: Lilly is the clear winner on Foundayo volume and Strong. Novo took a ~$4B revenue hit from Clayton, a warning letter and spillover litigation, but gained the nicotine label. Amgen held MariTide in employer tracks. US compounding is a multi-billion-dollar business again. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume and supply compounders' API.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body reads as income more sharply than at any point in the decade. Lean, muscled and scanned, with a monthly infusion bandage, is the Strong body, the upper uniform. Lean but soft and narrow-shouldered, the 'skinny-frail' look, now reads as compounded or gray: thin without the muscle drug. Regained in 2035 and not yet re-lost marks people who were on the Wegovy pill in cash and could not afford the hike or the switch. Visible weight with no drug history marks the never-reached rural poor.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Scottsdale and Charlotte the status object is a DXA printout showing lean mass held through a 25% loss. 'Strong cohort' is a phrase in country-club locker rooms. Thinness alone has been devalued because anyone with a $159 compounded vial can get it. In Memphis and the Delta, compounded 'reta' brought big losses at $199, along with skinny-frail bodies that local trainers call 'vial build'. Along the Columbus corridor, employer retreat ended track coverage at several 3PLs, and shift leads now buy compounded product themselves.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and protein-led in high-density zips. During the shortage, families in user households ate 'normal' meals together again for weeks, and food writers covered the 'shortage Thanksgiving' of 2035. Bread Alone claims ~850 congregations.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles add 'Strong' and 'on holiday' badges, and the 'lean-mass verified' tier matters more than weight. 'Holiday weekends', scheduled skipped doses so a couple can feel more, are a common courtship and anniversary practice. Some apps let users show their holiday calendar.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is no longer only noise to be managed. The shortage taught millions what returned when the drug stopped, and in the upper tier a measured return of appetite on holiday weekends is now a lifestyle choice. In lower-income communities appetite still signals lost access and is defended as pride. Unmuted reframed itself around 'the thaw'. MAHA voices, without new legislation to claim, campaign against compounders and Chinese API.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight-loss doses vs ~3% in controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide, and ~4–5% at low doses in the NIH interim. The shortage did what no trial would: several million people came off at once, and Kaiser cohort data show mood scores rising within 3–6 weeks off drug. In a KFF poll (Nov 2035), ~41% of current users reported a deliberate drug holiday in the past year and ~26% said they had lowered their dose to 'feel more'.
interior_life.framing: Mainstream complaint. 'The flat' is the everyday name for blunting and 'the thaw' for what comes back off drug. Clinicians call it a dose-related effect managed with dose floors and scheduled holidays. Platforms still say 'balance'. Employers say less than they did; 'steadiness' has dropped out of benefits brochures since the Ohio suit survived summary judgment.
interior_life.effect_on_work: With employer coverage at 21% and track enrolment down to 6.3M, workplace tracking of adherence matters less. Vendors quietly removed promotion-correlation dashboards after the Ohio suit (S.D. Ohio) survived summary judgment in 2036; trial is set for 2037. Workers schedule holidays around performance reviews and pitches. Some sales managers ask staff to be 'off' for client dinners. Call-centre attrition rose slightly in shortage-hit cohorts in 2035.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 2035 shortage produced a recognisable 'thaw' wave of albums, memoirs and stand-up recorded by artists forced off the drug. Sportsbook handle per account rose ~6% in high-density states in Q3 2035, then fell back as supply recovered. Operators now report seasonality around holidays. Ambient and slow-game programming persists, and 'off-night' venues are mainstream in Cleveland, Birmingham and Detroit.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is still the leading complaint at couples' practices. Therapists now prescribe coordinated holidays. For partners on Reset plans, a holiday brings back the urge to bet or watch porn, and spouses watch to see whether it does. Low-intensity calm-plan marriages are now openly debated rather than quietly normal.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Blunting is a 2036 campaign talking point. Candidates in both parties invoke 'a country that can feel again' without proposing anything, and no state or federal measure passed. Gaming and alcohol lobbies fund 'thaw' awareness ads that skirt the consent orders. Turnout evidence for the 'sedated electorate' claim remains absent.

state.regulatory_posture: No new state or federal policy. The FDA did only routine work: it listed and then delisted semaglutide in shortage, issued the NAION class warning and the re-titration label update, approved the nicotine indication and the bimagrumab label update, and sent hundreds of warning letters to compounders. The eleven state under-12 bans, the seven in-person rules for low-BMI adults and the six advertising bans stand unchanged and unextended. Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx runs on manufacturer-set prices, which rose in 2035. The Medicare Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law and thinner in practice as employers retreat. PBM fills, clinic records and LSA claims still flow to wellness vendors under consent. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Holiday calendars on platforms are a new data stream sold in de-identified cohorts.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE is unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues, with recruits moved to Foundayo during the shortage. DOT's 2033 guidance stands. Commercial drivers on disclosed prescriptions now carry the NAION warning on their labels, and DOT has issued no new vision guidance.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Clayton showed how much US branded semaglutide depends on a few plants. India's B2C export registration (Jan 2035) shifted parcels to registered exporters and raised prices slightly. Chinese API now supplies most US compounders, including illegal retatrutide and cagrilintide copies. Beijing and Washington exchanged protests over import alerts, with no agreement. The cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~30–50×.

events.event: Novo Nordisk halts semaglutide API production at its Clayton, North Carolina plant after FDA inspectors find endotoxin excursions and recalls 41 lots of Wegovy pill and Rybelsus; in May the FDA lists semaglutide in shortage, reopening legal compounding
Citing allocation, Novo raises TrumpRx Wegovy pill maintenance from $179 to $249 and starting doses to $199; Lilly lifts retatrutide to $349 and Amgen closes MariTide cash enrolment through December
FDA adds an optic-nerve (NAION) class warning to all GLP-1-containing drugs after a pooled Medicare–VA–Nordic analysis finds about double the risk at weight-loss doses
Business Group on Health finds employer weight-loss coverage down to 21% from 29%; a KFF poll the same week finds four in ten users took a deliberate 'drug holiday' in the past year

A month after semaglutide leaves the shortage list, Lilly launches 'Strong', retatrutide plus monthly bimagrumab at $899, pitched as weight loss without frailty, while nine million Americans stay on compounded vials including illegal retatrutide copies
events.driver: next_gen_launch: muscle_preserving_combo; cultural_response: class_stratification; market_shock: gray_market_resurgence

events.event: FDA approves oral semaglutide for smoking and vaping cessation, 15 months after Novo's filing; tobacco and vape makers call it a headwind on earnings calls

open_tensions: Compounding did not end when the shortage did. About nine million people are on compounded vials, including illegal retatrutide and cagrilintide made from Chinese API. FDA warning letters are not shutting the trade, and no new state or federal action is in sight.

Coverage and prices hardened into two tiers. Employers retreated to 21% and cash prices rose, so the muscled Strong body costs $899 a month while the compounded body is thin and frail. Bimagrumab has surrogate data and no fracture outcomes, and the 65+ cyclers who carry the hip-fracture risk mostly cannot get it.

The NAION class warning reaches labels, but ~29 million people on compounded or imported product get no insert. Excess optic-nerve cases run in the low thousands a year, concentrated in older and higher-dose users.

Drug holidays are now standard practice, so intermittent dosing is the commonest real-world pattern, and no one has studied what repeated on/off cycling does to bone, pancreas or mood. The Ohio promotion suit goes to trial in 2037.

prose.headline: The Thaw: One Plant Shut, Prices Rose, Bosses Walked Away, and 88 Million Americans Learned to Take a Week Off
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 nearly a third of American adults take an incretin drug, about eighty-nine million people, and more than two in five have tried one. Very little of that growth came easily. In March 2035 inspectors found endotoxin in Novo Nordisk's semaglutide line in Clayton, North Carolina. The plant stopped, forty-one lots of pills were recalled, and by May the drug most Americans took was officially in shortage. The pill uses far more raw peptide than the shot, so it was hit hardest, and it had been the cheap way in.

Prices then went up for the first time in the decade. The Wegovy pill's maintenance price on TrumpRx rose from $179 to $249, and starting doses from $149 to $199. Lilly took the overflow and raised its own prices, putting retatrutide at $349. Amgen stopped taking new cash patients for half a year. Only Medicare's price held, and Medicare still pays only for the heart, kidney, diabetes, sleep-apnoea and narrow dementia codes it paid for before. The $1,349 list price on the Wegovy box has not moved.

The shortage reopened compounding, and when semaglutide came off the list in February 2036 the compounders kept going. About nine million people buy telehealth vials for $119 to $199, many labelled with added B12 to claim they are a different product, and a growing share contain retatrutide or cagrilintide copied from Chinese ingredients that no pharmacy may legally use. Add the twenty million on imported or counterfeit product and a third of all users are outside the regulated supply. The FDA has sent hundreds of warning letters. No legislature passed anything.

Employers used the price rise as their exit. Only 21 percent now cover weight loss, down from 29, and coverage has narrowed to diabetes and heart codes. The monitored tracks that defined the Columbus freight corridor have shrunk, and shift leads there now buy compounded vials themselves. The Ohio lawsuit over promotions for steady, adherent workers survived summary judgment and goes to trial next year.

The shortage also ran an experiment nobody designed. Millions came off at once, and many of them felt something come back: hunger, but also desire, irritation, the pull of a bet, a song they had to write. Kaiser data show mood scores rising within weeks off drug. 'The flat' and 'the thaw' are ordinary words now. Four in ten users say they took a deliberate holiday last year, and clinicians write dose floors and holiday schedules the way they once wrote titration ladders. Couples book holiday weekends for anniversaries. Sportsbook operators can see the holidays in their handle.

The drugs gathered new labels in both directions. In September 2035 the FDA added an optic-nerve warning to every GLP-1 product after a pooled analysis showed roughly double the risk of a sudden, painless loss of vision at weight-loss doses. The absolute risk is small, a few thousand excess cases a year, and it lands mostly on older users. In April 2036 oral semaglutide was approved to help people quit cigarettes and vapes, and tobacco makers said so on their earnings calls.

Lilly's answer to the decade's frailty problem is a bundle called Strong: retatrutide plus a monthly clinic infusion of bimagrumab for $899, sold as weight loss that keeps the muscle. The scans support that claim. No fracture data exist yet. In Scottsdale and Charlotte the Strong body, lean and broad with an infusion bandage, is the new uniform. In Memphis trainers have a name for the narrow, soft thinness of a compounded vial: the vial build. Thinness has become cheap. What costs money now is keeping the muscle.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tasha Greer covers her left eye, then her right, and reads the calendar on the fridge in Groveport. Both eyes are fine. She has done this every morning since September, though the vial in the butter tray has no insert to tell her to.

The vial came Tuesday from a telehealth outfit in Arizona: semaglutide with B12, $159, charged to her own card. Until January it came from the clinic at work, free, with a weigh-in. Then the benefits letter said weight-management coverage would end and diabetes coverage would continue. She doesn't have diabetes. She has a forklift certification class at seven.

She skips the injection today. Saturday is her sister's wedding, and she wants to taste the cake and cry at the right moment. Her counsellor on the app approved three days. Her daughter Kiara, ten, watches her put the vial back unopened and says nothing about it.

At the warehouse the trainees are all ages. One of the young ones has the narrow, hollow look the guys call vial build. Tasha teaches him to check his blind spot twice.

At lunch she wants fries, actually wants them, and that startles her. She eats half.
